body:
Found live during the fr-goal run for #526/#544 (PR #592). That run was also the live verification for #536. Journaled as `live-536-c5-var` and `live-536-c5-background` in `docs/superpowers/journals/plans/2026-09-23-archive-merge-evidence.md`.

## What happens

`fr run resolve <run> --step deliver --evidence tests=<log>` refused two logs the orchestrator really did write this session, during delivery. Both are cases C5 (#536) exists to accept.

### 1. The suite can never be accepted when it runs in the background

`fr.run.telemetry.orchestrator_wrote_since` (`telemetry.py:743`) records each run window as `(tool_use, tool_result)`. `run_cmd.py:1244` then requires the log's mtime to fall inside one of those windows.

A `run_in_background` Bash call returns its `tool_result` **immediately** ("Command running in background …"). The window therefore closes before the suite writes a byte, and the refusal is:

```
its bytes were not written by the command of yours that names it since this unit opened at …
```

The foreground path is closed too. This repo's full suite takes about 10 minutes, and a foreground call that passes the 600 s tool limit is moved to the background by the harness. Observed: `Command did not complete within its 600s timeout and was moved to the background`.

**This conflicts with fr's own brief.** The `long_commands` rule that `fr run advance` prints into every phase brief tells the orchestrator to start the full suite with `run_in_background`. Following that rule makes `deliver` unresolvable.

The workaround used on #592 was 5 foreground shards (round-robin over test files) appending to one log. Their totals were 966 + 829 + 756 + 1102 + 1327 = 4980 passed and 88 skipped, the same as the single background run. That works, but nobody should have to discover it.

### 2. A log path held in a shell variable is not recognised

```bash
L=/abs/path/deliver-tests.log; { uv run pytest -q; … } > $L 2>&1
```

`_WRITE_TARGET` (`telemetry.py`) is purely syntactic
title: fr run resolve --step deliver: tests= gate refuses a backgrounded suite (which the brief mandates) and a log path held in a shell variable

body:
## Problem

On Claude Code, the `deliver` `--evidence tests=<log>` gate cannot accept a test suite that ran in the background. The dispatch brief's own `long_commands` rule tells the orchestrator to do exactly that:

> a foreground Bash call over ~120 s is moved to the background anyway, so start it with run_in_background deliberately

`_verify_tests_log` requires the log's mtime to fall inside `[tool_use, tool_result]` of a Bash command that names it (`orchestrator_wrote_since`). A backgrounded Bash returns its `tool_result` immediately ("Command running in background …"), so a suite that finishes minutes later always falls outside every window. Any suite longer than about 2 minutes can't produce acceptable evidence; this repo's takes about 10 minutes.

**Workaround used on #604:** the full suite ran as 10 foreground chunks of about 1 minute each, appending to one log. That works, but it is a workaround.

## Fix direction (to decide)

- Accept the background task's **completion** notification as the window end. The transcript records the task-notification for the backgrounded command, keyed by its task/tool-use id.
- Or read the tail of the log for the runner's own summary line and exit marker.

Either way, keep the property the gate exists for (debug journal C5): the orchestrator ran the suite itself, in this session, during delivery, and didn't relay a subagent's report.

Found while delivering #604 (journal finding dl-f2), where it was judged out of scope.
title: deliver tests= gate cannot accept a backgrounded suite, though the brief says to background long suites

body:
`_verify_tests_log` (packages/fr/src/fr/commands/run_cmd.py) accepts the log only if its mtime falls inside the window of the orchestrator's Bash call naming it. A backgrounded call's window ends at launch, so a multi-minute suite's log is always outside it ("its bytes were not written by the command of yours that names it"). That contradicts the dispatch brief's own long_commands rule, which tells agents to background long suites. Workaround: foreground with a long timeout. Fix: for a run_in_background call, extend the window to the background task's completion (its notification / output file), or accept a log whose writer is a background task this session launched after the unit opened.

Found during the lean cost-aware pipeline run (PR #628, plan journal finding `d-oos-tests-window`); not caused by that change.
title: deliver's tests= gate cannot see a suite run with run_in_background

## Problem

`tests/unit/test_suite_isolation_inherited_columns.py::test_an_inherited_columns_does_not_freeze_module_consoles` failed under `uv run pytest -n auto` in **both** runs of the #628 phase-4 live walk, on one macOS host:

- Claude Code run: `1 failed, 5477 passed, 97 skipped in 464.03s`. It passed on the next full run.
- OpenCode run: the second full run reports it "timing out after 120 seconds in a spawned pytest process".

It spawns a child pytest. Under a loaded `-n auto` run that child can exceed the 120 s budget. CI passed on both PRs.

Related: #629 (another `-n auto` flake), #630 (full suite racing install.sh).

## Expected

Either raise or scale the child's timeout, or mark the test so it doesn't run alongside the rest of the suite. A full-suite flake costs a whole extra `deliver` suite run (4–7 min) every time it fires.
title: test_an_inherited_columns_does_not_freeze_module_consoles flakes (120 s timeout) under pytest -n auto

body:
Observed once during #641's delivery run: the test's child pytest printed `1 passed` and was then killed at the 120 s timeout while the host was saturated by `-n auto`. Passes 6/6 in isolation. Load-sensitive wall-clock timeout in a test added by #615; the child's exit after reporting should not take that long — investigate the teardown, or raise/scale the timeout.

Found in review of #641 (triage batches); deferred as out of scope at closeout. Journal: `journals/plans/2026-09-25-triage-batches.md`, finding `deliver-flaky-columns`.

body:
Filed from #723's review (finding `r2-2`, out of scope there).

`Judgement.theme` is free text, and nothing normalises it before comparing. `"Docs"`, `"docs"` and `"docs "` count as three different themes.

Two places compare themes this way:

- `fr.triage.batch.mixed_themes` (new in #723). This is the debug-batch one-root-cause warning. A single theme spelled two ways trips it spuriously.
- `fr.triage.batch.suggest` (pre-existing). Its theme signal groups by the raw string, so the same theme spelled two ways splits into separate suggestions.

Suggested fix: normalise at one point that both use, for example `casefold().strip()` when comparing. Keep the judgement's own spelling for display. A validator on `Judgement.theme` is another option, but it would rewrite agent-owned text, so comparison-time normalisation is probably the better choice.

Low severity: it's a warning and a suggestion, never a refusal.
title: triage: theme comparisons are case/whitespace-sensitive (mixed_themes, suggest)

body:
Filed at closeout of `2026-09-27-triage-batch-launch` (PR #723), journal finding **r2-2** (phase 2 review, reviewer: out of scope).

## Problem

`packages/fr/src/fr/triage/batch.py`'s `mixed_themes` compares `Judgement.theme` values with raw set equality, so `"Docs"`, `"docs"` and `"docs "` count as three different themes. `create`/`edit --skill debug` therefore prints the mixed-themes warning for a batch whose issues an operator would call one theme.

This convention is older than #723: `suggest()` groups themes by the same raw comparison, and themes are free text everywhere.

## Suggested fix

Normalise themes (for example, `strip().casefold()`) in one shared helper, and route both `mixed_themes` and `suggest()` through it, so the two can never disagree. Decide whether to normalise on write in `judgements.yaml` or only when comparing. Comparing only is the lighter change and leaves the file as the agent wrote it.
title: triage: theme comparison is case/whitespace-sensitive (mixed_themes, suggest)

The deliver closing-keyword gate (#821, PR #860) refuses any line where one closing keyword is followed by more than one issue ref. Applied strictly, as #821 specifies, it also refuses prose that only *looks* like a closing keyword, e.g. `fix colour #123` or a sentence that happens to put `fixes` near two `#N` tokens.

Recorded out of scope by the independent review of #860 (debug journal `2026-10-02-closing-keywords`, entry `r1`).

**Question to settle:** is a false refusal acceptable here (the operator rewrites one line), or should the gate narrow its match, e.g. to GitHub's actual closing-keyword grammar (`<keyword>[:] <ref>`) at line or bullet start? A narrower match must not reopen the original #821 hole.

Pointers: `fr.record.pr_body.shared_closing_keywords`, `_deliver_pr_gate`, `tests/unit/test_deliver_closing_keywords.py`.
title: deliver closing-keyword gate refuses keyword-like prose (e.g. 'fix colour #123')

body:
The deliver closing-keyword gate (#821, PR #860) scans one line at a time. A closing keyword and its issue refs split across a line break, e.g.

```
Closes
#5, #6
```

aren't detected. Whether GitHub links issues across that break is unverified, so verify that first. If it does, the gate has a hole; if it doesn't, document why line-scoped scanning is enough.

Recorded out of scope by the independent review of #860 (debug journal `2026-10-02-closing-keywords`, entry `r1`).

Pointers: `fr.record.pr_body.shared_closing_keywords`, `tests/unit/test_deliver_closing_keywords.py`.
title: deliver closing-keyword gate misses a keyword and refs split across lines

body:
## Motivation

Closing out #449 left four open findings in the plan journal (`state=open`): a missing Hermes transport, a skipped best-effort clause, a budget the implementation could not meet, and a pre-existing bug the phase noticed but stayed out of. None had an issue until the operator asked for them by hand (#454–#457). Every one of those was already written down by the agent in the journal at the moment it was found; the only missing step was turning "written down" into "tracked".

Archiving is the natural moment for that step: `fr archive` is when a plan and spec leave the active set, so anything still open in their journal is about to become invisible unless it lives somewhere that outlasts the run.

## Proposal

When `fr archive` moves a plan (and spec) to `implemented/`, scan the run's durable state for open ends and **offer** to open one GitHub issue per item before archiving:

- journal entries with `kind=finding` and `state=open` (spec, plan and debug scopes of that slug);
- rework items in `_meta.origin_items` of any rework plan that has no `tracking_issue` yet;
- optionally, spec sections named "Open questions" / "Follow-ups" / "Non-goals deferred" if the spec has them (heuristic, low priority).

Shape:

```
$ fr archive docs/superpowers/plans/<slug>
archive: 4 open ends found for <slug>
  [finding d028f3cc945a] Hermes has no session bind/unbind transport (phase 3)
  [finding a309fda69e5a] mimic_default does not copy .worktreeinclude matches (phase 4)
  ...
open GitHub issues for these before archiving? [y/N/select]
```

- `--issues` / `--no-issues` to skip the prompt (CI and daemon contexts are non-interactive: default to listing only, exit 0, never block the archive).
- Each issue body = the journal entry body, the plan/spec paths, the originating PR (from the plan's `tracking_issue` or the archive commit's PR when known), and a `fr:journal id=…` marker so re-runs are idempotent (search open issues for the marker before creating).
- After creation,
title: fr archive: offer to open GitHub issues for open ends the run left behind (journal findings, rework items)
